findings.recommendation: No action required for markers. Optionally convert the two real budget TODOs into GitHub issues so they stop living as comments, and `rmdir` the two empty worktree dirs.

findings.title: JWT access_token serialized into page HTML via define:vars on 6 surfaces, defeating httpOnly
findings.description: Six rendered surfaces read the httpOnly access_token cookie server-side and serialize the raw JWT into an inline <script> in the delivered HTML: pages/parent/settings/a2a.astro:59 (`<script type="module" define:vars={{ token, lang }}>` with `const token = Astro.cookies.get("access_token")?.value` at line 9), pages/budget/scan-receipt.astro:238, pages/budget/transactions.astro:606, pages/budget/settings.astro:578, components/TaskCreateModal.astro:411 (token passed as a prop from pages/parent/tasks.astro:558), and components/RecycleBinTable.astro:191 (`define:vars={{ token: session.token }}` from pages/budget/recycle-bin/index.astro:51). The scripts then send `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` on client fetches. This defeats the app's own security design: the cookie is set httpOnly (middleware.ts:304-310) precisely so browser JS cannot read it, and the same-origin proxy (pages/api/budget/[...path].ts:30-37) already extracts the cookie server-side and injects the Authorization header — its comment states "The access_token cookie is httpOnly so browser JS cannot read it." With CSP allowing `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` (middleware.ts:21), any HTML-injection XSS can read the token straight out of the DOM and exfiltrate a fully valid API credential; the token also persists in saved pages and disk cache. (kiosk.astro's define:vars token is the kiosk device token from the URL, not the JWT — excluded.)
findings.evidence: a2a.astro:9 `const token = Astro.cookies.get("access_token")?.value;` → line 59 `<script type="module" define:vars={{ token, lang }}>`; proxy [...path].ts:31-32 "The access_token cookie is httpOnly so browser JS cannot read it. Extract it server-side and inject as Authorization header if not already set."
findings.recommendation: Drop `token` from every define:vars/prop on these 6 surfaces and delete the client-side `Authorization: Bearer` headers — the /api/* proxy already injects the header from the cookie when the client omits it (it only skips injection `if (!forwardHeaders.has("Authorization"))`). Verify the multipart upload paths (scan-receipt, TaskCreateModal proof upload) still authenticate through the cookie path, then add a lint/grep CI guard against `define:vars={{ token` reappearing.

findings.title: Shopping list check-off is a full form-POST/redirect/SSR reload per item, with write errors silently swallowed
findings.description: shopping.astro is the only interactive domain page with zero client-side JS (grep `fetch(` = 0). Every action — checking off an item in the store, adding an item, deleting — is a `<form method="POST">` handled in frontmatter, followed by `Astro.redirect("/shopping…")` (line 76) and a full SSR re-render (auth/me + lists + list detail = 3 API round trips). Checking off 10 grocery items = 10 full page reloads, each losing scroll position on a long list — this is the single most-repeated in-store interaction in the app. Worse, the `toggle_item`, `delete_item`, `archive_list`, and `delete_list` branches (lines 40-75) discard the apiFetch result entirely (only create_list/add_item set `errorMsg`), so a failed toggle (offline in a store with bad reception is the common case) redirects anyway and renders the item unchanged with zero feedback. Sibling daily-use pages (chat reactions, gigs claims, bank) use the shared `mutate()` optimistic helper.
findings.evidence: Lines 43-49: `if (itemId) { await apiFetch(`/api/shopping/items/${itemId}`, { method: "PATCH", token, body: JSON.stringify({ is_checked: !checked }) }); }` — return value ignored, no errorMsg; line 251: `<form method="POST" class="flex-1 flex items-center gap-3">` wrapping each item's check-off button; line 76 unconditional redirect.
findings.recommendation: Convert item check-off and delete to `mutate()` with optimistic strike-through + revert-on-error (the exact pattern already live in gigs/index.astro and bank.astro), keeping the form POST as no-JS fallback. At minimum, capture the apiFetch error in the toggle/delete branches so failures surface in the existing errorMsg banner.

findings.title: Kiosk auto-refresh via location.reload() every 60s bricks the wall tablet on any transient network failure
findings.description: The kiosk board — designed as an always-on shared wall display — refreshes by reloading the entire page every 60 seconds. If the reload happens during a Wi-Fi blip, tunnel hiccup, or backend deploy, the browser lands on its native error page (or the SW offline fallback), the inline script with the interval is gone, and the kiosk stays dead until a human walks over and manually reloads it. The data needed for refresh is already available as JSON at `/api/kiosk/snapshot?token=…` (the frontmatter fetches it at line 16-18); a fetch-then-patch (or even fetch-success-then-reload) approach would make the board self-heal through outages instead of dying on the first one.
findings.evidence: kiosk.astro:355-359: `// Auto-refresh every 60s to pull the latest snapshot...` `setInterval(() => { if (!overlayOpen()) location.reload(); }, 60_000);`
findings.recommendation: Minimal fix: `fetch(location.href, {method:'HEAD'})` (or the snapshot endpoint) first and only call `location.reload()` on success, silently retrying next tick on failure. Better: fetch `/api/kiosk/snapshot` and re-render the board sections client-side, which also stops the visible white-flash reload on the wall display.

findings.title: Page-level modals lack dialog semantics, Escape handling, and focus management that component modals already implement
findings.description: The design-system modals (FABModal, TaskCreateModal, MoreSheet, DrawerMenu, AccountCreateModal, ui/BottomSheet) all ship `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"`, Escape-to-close, and focus moves/trap (e.g. MoreSheet.astro:209 implements a real shift-Tab wrap). But the hand-rolled page-level modals do none of it: pages/bank.astro:299 (#bank-modal) and :325 (#goal-modal), pages/gigs/index.astro:247 (#propose-modal), pages/parent/gigs.astro:411 (#gig-modal), pages/parent/settings/family-bank.astro:452/:490, pages/parent/tasks.astro:380 (#preview-modal), pages/parent/assignments.astro:506, pages/budget/settings.astro:535/:559, pages/parent/settings/mcp-tokens.astro:184, components/EditMemberModal.astro:17, components/InvitationModal.astro:25, components/MoveMoneyModal.astro:24, components/RecycleBinTable.astro:110/137/164 — a grep for `keydown|Escape|role="dialog"|aria-modal` across these files returns nothing. Screen-reader users get no dialog announcement and background content stays in the reading order; keyboard users cannot dismiss with Escape and focus stays behind the backdrop.
findings.evidence: bank.astro:299 `<div id="bank-modal" class="hidden fixed inset-0 z-[60] flex items-end sm:items-center justify-center bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-sm px-4">` — no role, no aria-modal, no keydown handler anywhere in the file; contrast FABModal.astro:32-33 `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`.
findings.recommendation: Extract the open/close + Escape + initial-focus + focus-restore logic already proven in MoreSheet/FABModal into a tiny shared helper (or migrate these modals onto the orphaned ui/BottomSheet.astro, which already implements all of it), and add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby` to each container.

findings.title: 70 location.reload()-after-write sites remain; parent routine builder reloads the whole page on every step edit
findings.description: The shared mutate() helper (lib/mutate.ts) was introduced to end reload-after-write, and its docstring still claims "~30 location.reload() calls" — the actual count is now 70 across pages/, and only 4 pages import mutate. The worst daily-felt case is the parent routine builder: creating a routine, toggling active, deleting a routine, deleting a step, and adding a step EACH trigger `location.reload()` (parent/routines.astro:290, 305, 317, 330, 352). Building a 6-step morning routine costs 6+ full SSR reloads, each scrolling back to the top and re-fetching the whole page — while sibling parent surfaces (approvals, gigs review) update the DOM in place. This is the same interaction class the 2026-07-02 UX-audit waves converted for chat/budget/gigs, so the app now trains users to expect instant feedback and then breaks that expectation on routines, family-cup, receipt-drafts, and subscription pages.
findings.evidence: parent/routines.astro:328-333: `await api("/api/routines/" + btn.dataset.rid + "/steps/" + btn.dataset.sid, { method: "DELETE" }); location.reload();` (one of 5 sites in the file); lib/mutate.ts:4 "The app has ~30 `location.reload()` calls after writes" vs `grep -rn "location.reload()" pages | wc -l` → 70.
findings.recommendation: Convert the routine builder's step add/delete and routine toggle/delete to in-place DOM updates via mutate() (remove the <li>, update the toggle chip). Sweep the remaining reload sites opportunistically, prioritizing kid-facing routines.astro:306 and receipt-drafts. Update the stale count in mutate.ts's docstring.

findings.title: Divergent feedback patterns: native alert()/confirm() on ~60 sites vs styled toast/confirm dialogs on sibling pages
findings.description: The same interactions get three different treatments depending on the page. Delete confirmation: budget/settings.astro:559 built a styled #confirm-overlay dialog with branded buttons, while budget/transactions.astro:1220 (`confirm(es ? "¿Eliminar ${picked.size} transacciones?...")`), budget/reports.astro:703, chat.astro:416, and ~25 other sites use `window.confirm` — which on the installed PWA renders a jarring browser-chrome dialog ("family.agent-ia.mx says…"). Error/success feedback: a global ToastContainer + showToast exist and are used by bank/gigs/pet/routines, but budget/transactions.astro alone has 15+ `alert()` calls (676, 703, 1087, 1096-1101, 1126-1131, 1207-1229, 1278, 1289), chat.astro alerts on edit/delete failure (411, 421) despite using mutate-with-toast for reactions in the same file, and budget/settings.astro built its own private #settings-toast (line 575) instead of importing the shared one. Kids and parents see native OS dialogs on money flows and polished toasts everywhere else.
findings.evidence: budget/transactions.astro:1220 `if (!confirm(es ? \`¿Eliminar ${picked.size} transacciones? (van a la papelera)\` : ...)) return;` vs budget/settings.astro:559-571 styled `#confirm-overlay` dialog for the identical delete-confirmation interaction; chat.astro:411 `alert(isEs ? "No se pudo editar el mensaje." : ...)` in the same file that imports mutate/showToast (line 342).
findings.recommendation: Promote budget/settings.astro's confirm-overlay into a shared `confirmDialog()` component/helper and swap the window.confirm sites onto it (budget + chat first). Replace alert() error feedback with the existing showToast — mutate() already does this automatically, so many sites collapse into mutate() calls.

findings.title: Dynamically-created icon-only buttons (✕ close/delete) missing aria-label
findings.description: Several icon-only buttons created in JS template strings or via createElement ship no accessible name: budget/transactions.astro:637 (split-row delete `✕` in the split-editor template), transactions.astro:1255-1257 (saved-filter chip delete, `del.textContent = "✕"` with no aria-label), budget/reports.astro:154 (#cr-output-close `✕`), reports.astro:699-701 (custom-report chip delete), components/BudgetNavNew.astro:190 (undo-snackbar dismiss `✕`). Screen readers announce these as unlabeled 'button'. The codebase knows the right pattern — GuideShell.astro:162-164 labels its identical `✕`/zoom buttons, and shopping.astro's `×` delete has aria-label="Delete" — so this is drift in the newer budget surfaces. Several are also below the 44px touch-target floor (`text-[10px] -ml-1` on the chip deletes).
findings.evidence: transactions.astro:637 `<button type="button" class="split-del text-red-400 hover:text-red-600 text-sm">✕</button>` and 1255-1257 `del.className = "text-[10px] text-brand-ink-soft hover:text-red-600 -ml-1"; del.textContent = "✕";` — no aria-label; contrast GuideShell.astro:164 `<button type="button" data-act="close" aria-label="Close">✕</button>`.
findings.recommendation: Add lang-appropriate `aria-label` (and `p-2`/min-size padding for touch targets) to the 5 listed buttons — pure additive one-line changes.

findings.title: A2A webhook settings form: no error catch on network failure and no double-submit protection
findings.description: The Price Agent settings form is the only client-side submit handler in the app with neither a try/catch nor a submit-button disable (every other checked form — register, bank, gigs, InvitationModal, EditMemberModal, MoveMoneyModal — disables its button and catches). A network failure during `fetch("/api/budget/a2a-webhook", {method:"PUT"…})` throws an unhandled rejection: the button silently does nothing, and the parent can double-tap Save, racing two PUTs — dangerous here specifically because `rotate_secret: true` mints a new webhook secret, so a double-fire can rotate twice and display a stale secret the user then copies into their agent config.
findings.evidence: a2a.astro:60-71 — `document.getElementById("form")?.addEventListener("submit", async (e) => { e.preventDefault(); const resp = await fetch("/api/budget/a2a-webhook", { method: "PUT", ... });` — no try/catch anywhere in the handler, and the submit button (line 49) is never disabled.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the handler in try/catch with an error message, and disable the submit button for the duration of the request (restore in finally) — the pattern is copy-pasteable from bank.astro:459-478. Combine with the token-embed removal (finding 1) since it touches the same script block.

findings.title: Deploy 'smoke check' never fails the deploy; tunnel is excluded from every health gate
findings.description: verify_public() curls the two public URLs but only echoes the HTTP code — it never asserts success, never returns non-zero, and runs after the rollback decision has already been made. Meanwhile wait_healthy (line 105) polls only db/redis/backend/frontend; family_onprem_tunnel has no healthcheck in docker-compose.onprem.yml (lines 129-150) and is not in the wait list. So the exact failure mode this host has already exhibited (cloudflared HTTP 530 when the egress-net DNS pin is lost) sails through: containers healthy, script prints 'Deploy complete', public site down. CLAUDE.md advertises that the script 'smoke-checks the public endpoints', which overstates what the code does.
findings.evidence: deploy-onprem.sh:168-169: `code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$url" 2>/dev/null || echo 000); echo "$url → $code"` — code is captured, echoed, and discarded; the function unconditionally succeeds and line 421 prints 'Deploy complete.' regardless. wait_healthy:105 iterates only `family_onprem_db family_onprem_redis family_onprem_backend family_onprem_frontend`.
findings.recommendation: Make verify_public assert `code` is 200 (or <400) for both URLs, with a short retry loop for tunnel reconnect lag, and exit non-zero with a loud banner on failure (do not auto-rollback here — public failure with healthy containers is an ingress problem, not an image problem). Add a healthcheck to the tunnel service (run cloudflared with `--metrics 127.0.0.1:2000` and probe its /ready endpoint) and include family_onprem_tunnel in wait_healthy.

findings.title: Health gate is liveness-only: /health checks nothing, /ready exists but is never used by compose or deploy
findings.description: The backend container healthcheck — the sole trigger for the deploy script's automatic-rollback path — hits GET /health, which backend/app/main.py:428-431 documents as 'Cheap; does NOT touch dependencies'. A readiness probe /ready (main.py:434-472) that verifies DB and Redis connectivity and returns 503 on failure already exists but nothing consumes it. A deploy that ships code unable to talk to the DB (bad DATABASE_URL edit, pool/driver regression, Redis auth change) reports every container healthy, passes wait_healthy, skips rollback, and 500s on real traffic.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.onprem.yml:97: healthcheck urlopen("http://localhost:8000/health") vs main.py:430: "Liveness probe: the process is up. Cheap; does NOT touch dependencies." and main.py:436: "Readiness probe: can we actually serve — DB and Redis reachable?" — grep shows no other reference to /ready in compose or scripts.
findings.recommendation: Point the compose backend healthcheck at /ready (safe with restart: unless-stopped — podman marks unhealthy without restart-looping), or at minimum have deploy-onprem.sh's post-up gate curl the internal /ready before declaring success, so the automatic rollback can actually catch dependency-level breakage.

findings.title: Prod compose has no memory/CPU limits, no stop_grace_period, and no log-driver options on a shared 4-stack host
findings.description: None of the five services declares mem_limit/cpus (verified: grep for stop_grace_period|mem_limit|cpus|logging returns nothing). 10.1.0.91 is explicitly a SHARED box (school-admin, medical, platform, vault) — a leak in uvicorn/node or a runaway postgres query can pressure-OOM neighboring stacks, and the kernel OOM-killer picks the victim. Redis alone is bounded (--maxmemory 256mb via its command line). Separately, the default 10s SIGTERM→SIGKILL stop timeout hard-kills the backend while `scheduler.shutdown(wait=True)` (main.py:238) is draining a mid-flight money-moving sweep (payday sweep is idempotent per week, so it tolerates this, but in-flight Jarvis SSE/LLM responses up to LLM_TIMEOUT are simply severed on every deploy). Log rotation is also unconfigured and left to the host's podman default driver.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.onprem.yml services backend (54-101), frontend (103-127), postgres (16-33): no mem_limit, no cpus, no stop_grace_period, no logging: key anywhere in the file; only redis self-bounds via `--maxmemory 256mb` (line 43).
findings.recommendation: Add mem_limit (e.g. backend 1g, frontend 512m, postgres 1g) and a `stop_grace_period: 30s` on backend so uvicorn can drain SSE streams and the scheduler can finish a sweep. Set explicit `logging: driver/max-size` options (or verify journald rotation on the host) so backend logs can't fill the disk that also holds the postgres volume.

findings.title: LLM + server-side URL fetch endpoint /api/meals/recipes/import has no rate limit (every other LLM route does)
findings.description: All other LLM-invoking routes carry @limiter.limit(AI_LIMIT) (jarvis chat/chat-stream, calendar scan, task_templates, budget receipt scan — verified by grep), but the recipe importer route has only the premium gate. A single paid account can hammer LiteLLM unboundedly from one IP. It compounds: import_recipe_from_url() fetches the user-supplied URL server-side with follow_redirects=True and only a scheme check (recipe_importer.py:80-87) — no private-IP/SSRF guard — so the same unlimited endpoint is also a free proxy for probing the LAN/internal container networks from the backend's vantage point.
findings.evidence: meals.py:111-119: `@router.post("/recipes/import", ...)` → `await require_feature("ai_features", db, current_user)` with no @limiter.limit; recipe_importer.py:80-87: `if not url.startswith(("http://", "https://")) ... client.get(url)` with `follow_redirects=True`. Rate-limited route inventory via `grep -rn limiter.limit app/api/routes/` shows meals.py absent.
findings.recommendation: Add `@limiter.limit(AI_LIMIT)` (plus the `request: Request` param slowapi needs) to import_recipe. While there, reject URLs resolving to private/link-local address space before fetching, or route the fetch through an allowlist.

findings.title: Unauthenticated PayPal webhook amplifies each request into outbound PayPal API calls with no rate limit
findings.description: POST /api/subscriptions/webhook is public by design, and signature verification is delegated to PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API via asyncio.to_thread — meaning every spam request (garbage signatures included) costs this backend an outbound OAuth token fetch + verify call (15s timeouts each, paypal_service.py:55,94,114) and a slot in the default thread executor. A flood of junk POSTs can saturate the small default executor and starve other to_thread users (including legitimate webhook verification and PayPal cancel calls) before any 401 is returned. The webhook logic itself is well built — post-commit Redis dedupe, 503-for-retry on dispatch failure, double-billing operator flags — this is purely a front-door throttling gap.
findings.evidence: subscriptions_webhook.py:108-117: `verified = await asyncio.to_thread(PayPalService.verify_webhook_signature, ...)` on a route with no limiter decorator and no auth; paypal_service.py:257-260 posts to `/v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature` per call.
findings.recommendation: Add a generous per-IP slowapi limit (e.g. 120/minute — far above PayPal's real delivery rate, keyed on CF-Connecting-IP like the rest) and/or short-circuit before the PayPal round-trip when the paypal-transmission-* headers are absent/malformed.

findings.title: Dead JWT_SECRET_KEY in .env.onprem.example — never read by the app; SECRET_KEY is the real JWT signer
findings.description: The prod env template instructs the operator to generate three secrets, but `JWT_SECRET_KEY` does not exist in app/core/config.py and `grep -rn JWT_SECRET_KEY backend/app/` returns zero hits — JWTs are signed with SECRET_KEY (config.py:30, validated non-default at boot when DEBUG=false). The trap is operational: during an incident an operator 'rotating the JWT key' by changing JWT_SECRET_KEY rotates nothing, leaving possibly-compromised tokens valid while believing they were invalidated.
findings.evidence: .env.onprem.example:23-25 lists `SECRET_KEY=`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY=CHANGE_ME_openssl_rand_hex_32`, `SESSION_SECRET_KEY=`; config.py defines only SECRET_KEY (line 30) and SESSION_SECRET_KEY (line 37); no consumer of JWT_SECRET_KEY anywhere under backend/app/.
findings.recommendation: Delete the JWT_SECRET_KEY line from .env.onprem.example (and .env.example if present), or add a comment stating SECRET_KEY signs JWTs. Check the live .env on 10.1.0.91 for the same stray key so future rotation runbooks target SECRET_KEY.

findings.title: Destructive transaction dedup service has zero test coverage
findings.description: DeduplicateService (77 statements, 0.0% coverage in the 2026-07-26 full-suite run) is completely untested, yet it is a data-destructive money-adjacent path: it soft-deletes the 'loser' of each duplicate pair and transfers receipt_image_path to the winner. It is user-reachable via POST /api/budget/transactions/deduplicate (backend/app/api/routes/budget/transactions.py:194) with dry_run defaulting to False. The richness-scoring (_score), the both-have-images skip rule, the 1% amount tolerance, and the receipt-path transfer are all unverified. A scoring or tolerance regression would silently soft-delete the wrong transaction across every family that runs dedup.
findings.evidence: coverage htmlcov status.json: dedup_service_py stmts=77 miss=77 (0.0%). `grep -rn "DeduplicateService\|dedup_service" tests/` returns only the route import at app/api/routes/budget/transactions.py:205 — zero test references. Route: `@router.post("/deduplicate")` ... `result = await DeduplicateService.run(db, family_id, deleted_by_id=current_user.id, dry_run=dry_run)`.
findings.recommendation: Add tests/test_dedup_service.py covering: winner selection by richness score (receipt vs notes vs items vs CSV-import penalty), both-have-images pair skipped, ±1% amount tolerance boundary, split children and soft-deleted rows excluded, receipt path transferred to winner, dry_run=True mutates nothing, and family_id isolation (family B's identical transactions never merged). The existing transaction_factory_with_payee fixture in conftest.py already supports most of this.

findings.title: CI never runs tests against the migration-produced schema — model/migration drift ships green
findings.description: CI runs `alembic upgrade head` first, but conftest's session fixture then drops every table and rebuilds the schema from `Base.metadata.create_all` — so the entire 1900-test suite runs against the ORM-derived schema, never the migration-derived one, and no drift check (alembic check / compare_metadata) exists anywhere (`grep -rln compare_metadata tests/` is empty). A hand-written migration that misses a column, index, or enum value that the models define passes the round-trip AND the full test suite, and only fails when deploy-onprem.sh runs alembic against prod and the app 500s on the missing column.
findings.evidence: ci.yml:96-97 comment: "Safe before pytest: tests/conftest.py drops and recreates every table except alembic_version at session start." conftest.py:51-53 `await _drop_all_pg(pg)` then :92 `await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)`.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI step after `alembic upgrade head` that runs `alembic check` (alembic >= 1.9 autogenerate-diff; requires bumping the 1.13.1 pin's config only) or a small pytest that runs `compare_metadata()` against the migrated DB and asserts an empty diff. Alternatively make conftest build the schema via `alembic upgrade head` instead of metadata.create_all so every test exercises the real prod schema.

findings.title: TransferService money-movement paths at 16.7% coverage, zero direct tests
findings.description: transfer_between_accounts (creates paired ledger transactions), transfer_between_categories, and TransferService.cover_overspending are untested — 16.7% coverage is import-time lines only. test_cover_overspending.py tests AllocationService.cover_overspending, not this service, and no test references TransferService or the /api/budget/transfers routes at all. This is the service that moves user money between budget accounts; a sign error or unpaired-transaction bug would corrupt account balances family-wide with nothing failing in CI. The prior audit flagged its 10 HTTPException sites (known-open); the total absence of tests on it is a separate, unreported gap.
findings.evidence: coverage: transfer_service_py stmts=84 miss=70 (16.7%). `grep -rn "TransferService\|budget/transfers" tests/*.py` → only test_cover_overspending.py hits, all of which call `AllocationService.cover_overspending(...)` (lines 143-250), never TransferService.
findings.recommendation: Add tests/test_transfer_service.py: account→account transfer creates exactly two mirrored transactions with correct signs and shared transfer link, category transfer moves allocation amounts, insufficient-balance and cross-family refusals, and deletion/rollback symmetry. Do it before Jarvis MCP wires a 'transfer between accounts' tool (the audit's predicted breakage point).

findings.title: 70% global coverage gate hides critical modules at 0-40%
findings.description: The single global `--cov-fail-under=70` lets high-risk modules sit far below the gate indefinitely, subsidized by well-tested CRUD. From the 2026-07-26 run, the worst offenders on critical paths: budget/dedup_service 0%, schemas/validation.py 0%, budget/transfer_service 16.7%, task_proof_validator 29.4% (LLM gig-proof gate — only ever mocked, its parse/validation logic never executed), family_export_service 33.9% (GDPR-style export), routes/budget/bank_sync.py 38.2%, routes/budget/ai_settings.py 39.6% (zero test references at all), receipt_draft_service 43.7%, subscriptions route 45.2% (billing), gig_claim_service 56.4%, admin_action_service 56.5% (cross-tenant operator writes, one day old).
findings.evidence: htmlcov status.json sorted ascending (stmts>30): `0.0% dedup_service_py`, `16.7% transfer_service_py`, `29.4% task_proof_validator_py`, `33.9% family_export_service_py`, `38.2% bank_sync_py`, `39.6% ai_settings_py`, `45.2% subscriptions_py`, `56.5% admin_action_service_py`. `grep -rln "ai-settings\|ai_settings" tests/` → empty.
findings.recommendation: Keep the global gate but add per-path floors for money/AI/admin code (coverage's `fail_under` per-package isn't native — use diff-cover on PRs, or a small script asserting minimum coverage for app/services/budget, app/services/admin, app/services/bank_service.py from coverage.xml). Triage order: dedup_service, transfer_service, ai_settings routes, task_proof_validator's real parsing path.

findings.title: CI has no dependency-audit, secret-scanning, or Dependabot automation
findings.description: .github/ contains only workflows/ci.yml — no dependabot.yml, no pip-audit/npm audit step, no secret scanner (gitleaks/trufflehog). The prior audit already flagged the pins as stale (authlib 1.3.0, redis 5.0.1, fastapi 0.115.6 — known-open); what is new here is that nothing will ever notice when one of those pins gains a CVE, and a committed secret (this repo handles PayPal, LiteLLM, SMTP, OAuth keys in .env files) would land unreviewed. For a live billing product this is the cheapest missing safety net.
findings.evidence: `ls .github/ .github/workflows/` → only `workflows/ci.yml`; `cat .github/dependabot.yml` → no such file; ci.yml jobs are exactly `backend` (ruff/alembic/pytest) and `frontend` (npm ci/check/build) — no audit or scan steps.
findings.recommendation: Add (1) .github/dependabot.yml for pip + npm + github-actions ecosystems, weekly; (2) a non-blocking-then-blocking `pip-audit -r backend/requirements.txt` and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` job; (3) gitleaks action on push. All three are <30 lines of YAML total.

findings.title: Playwright e2e suite (30 specs) never runs in CI
findings.description: The e2e suite exists and covers real flows (auth refresh, middleware security headers, scanner-v2, kiosk, jarvis) but is wired only to a manually-started local Docker stack — no CI job references playwright at all. Combined with the project's documented history of stale-image local runs ('stale podman images test old code' memory), the suite only proves anything when someone remembers to rebuild and run it. Regressions in the frontend script islands and middleware are structurally invisible to CI (astro check is types-only).
findings.evidence: playwright.config.js:20-21 `// webServer is disabled since we're using the Docker-based dev stack`, baseURL `http://localhost:3003`; `grep -rn "playwright\|e2e" .github/workflows/ci.yml` → no matches.
findings.recommendation: Add a third CI job that brings up backend+frontend+postgres+redis via docker compose (or services + `npm run dev`), seeds via seed_data.py, and runs a tagged @smoke subset (login, dashboard, task complete, budget txn) — full suite nightly on a schedule rather than per-PR if runtime is a concern.

findings.title: Zero e2e coverage for admin console, bank, pet, meals, and budget import
findings.description: Mapping the 30 e2e specs against frontend/src/pages: the operator admin console (6 pages under /admin — index, families, families/[id], audit, billing-review, deletions; merged yesterday in PR #163) has no spec (kiosk-admin.spec.js is the kiosk device, not the operator console). Also uncovered: /bank (Family Bank money UI), /pet, /meals, /budget/import (CSV/OFX), /budget/receipt-drafts (HITL queue). pricing.spec.js is shallow — it asserts a redirect and that the plan table renders; no upgrade-flow interaction (consistent with the known 'first real payment untested' state, but the pre-PayPal UI steps are testable). The admin console is the sharpest gap: a cross-tenant surface whose frontend has never been driven end-to-end.
findings.evidence: `grep -ln "'/admin" e2e-tests/*.spec.js` → empty; same for `'/bank`, `'/pet`, `meals`. e2e-tests/ listing shows no bank/pet/meals/admin/import/receipt-drafts spec. pricing.spec.js tests: 'redirects to the canonical subscription settings page', 'shows the plan comparison table', plus an analytics CSV check — nothing further.
findings.recommendation: Priority order: (1) admin.spec.js — operator login via allowlisted superadmin, family directory renders, one bounded write action lands in the audit log view; (2) bank.spec.js — kid balance renders, parent releases allowance; (3) budget-import.spec.js — CSV upload happy path. Pet/meals can wait (pet feature itself is uncertain per project notes).

findings.title: New admin tests re-introduce the local-date week_of pattern PR #130 eliminated
findings.description: The chore-proportional release test (line 733) and the points_rate fault-injection test (line 877) — both written 2026-07-26 — seed money-bearing TaskAssignments with `week_of = date.today() - timedelta(days=today.weekday())` computed from the RUNNER's local clock, while BankService's release path computes the current week via `_family_local_today` (family tz, which defaults to UTC for the test_family fixture). On a UTC-6 dev machine any Sunday evening, local 'today' is Sunday but UTC is already Monday: the row lands in last week's bucket, the release finds zero chore units, and the 'money actually moved' / fault-injection-window asserts fail. This is exactly the evening/Sunday flake class root-caused and fixed in PR #130; the fixed suite (test_chore_paycheck.py) uses a `_current_week_monday` helper that calls `BankService._family_local_today` — the new tests didn't. CI (UTC runners) is safe; local runs are not, and this repo's convention is trusting the bare-metal local suite.
findings.evidence: test_admin_actions.py:732-733 `today = date.today()` / `week_monday = today - timedelta(days=today.weekday())` (again at 877-878), feeding a chore_proportional/points_rate release that asserts real money movement; vs bank_service.py:533 `async def _family_local_today(...)` and the sanctioned pattern at tests/test_chore_paycheck.py:47-54 `today = await BankService._family_local_today(db, family_id)`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the two inline computations with the `_current_week_monday(db, family_id)` helper from test_chore_paycheck.py (hoist it into conftest.py so the next test author finds it). Also note the suite has no freezegun/time-machine dependency at all — adopting one would retire this whole class.

findings.title: Frontend logic has zero unit tests; security middleware only covered by never-run e2e
findings.description: package.json has no test script and no test framework dependency — the frontend's only automated checks are `astro check` (types) and `astro build`. frontend/src/middleware.ts implements security-load-bearing logic (CSRF origin check, transparent token refresh, CSP headers, disabled-module deep-link bounce) whose only test is e2e-tests/middleware-security.spec.js — which, per the CI finding, never executes in CI. Net effect: the CSRF check could be inverted and every automated signal would stay green.
findings.evidence: frontend/package.json scripts: `"dev", "build", "check", "preview", "astro"` — no test entry; `grep vitest\|jest frontend/package.json` empty. middleware-security.spec.js exists but ci.yml contains no playwright job.
findings.recommendation: Add vitest with a handful of targeted unit tests for middleware.ts pure helpers (origin validation, protected-path matching, module-bounce logic) — Astro middleware is plain TS and testable without a browser. Wire `vitest run` into the frontend CI job. This is much cheaper than full e2e-in-CI and covers the highest-risk file.

findings.title: conftest db_session teardown swallows cleanup failures per-table
findings.description: The post-test cleanup loop wraps each `table.delete()` in `try/except Exception: pass`. Under asyncpg, one failed DELETE aborts the transaction, making every subsequent DELETE in the loop fail too — all silently — so the final commit either raises an opaque PendingRollbackError attributed to an unrelated test, or (if the first failure was pre-transactional) leaves rows that bleed into later tests. The comment claims the guard is for 'table might not exist', but sorted_tables comes from live metadata, so real failures it masks are FK violations or aborted-transaction cascades. Separately, Redis is never flushed between tests (sessions, kiosk prefs, per-family receipt-model keys persist for the whole run) — currently benign because family IDs are random UUIDs, worth a comment at minimum.
findings.evidence: conftest.py:126-134: `for table in reversed(Base.metadata.sorted_tables): ... try: await session.execute(table.delete()) except Exception: # Table might not exist if schema is being rebuilt pass` followed by an unguarded `await session.commit()`.
findings.recommendation: Drop the per-statement try/except and let a cleanup failure fail loudly at the offending table (or collect and re-raise with table names). Consider a single `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE` of all tables in one statement — faster and atomic. Add `flushdb` on the test Redis DB in an autouse fixture or a comment documenting why leakage is acceptable.

findings.title: app/schemas/validation.py is dead code — 0% coverage, imported nowhere
findings.description: Coverage data shows the module at 0.0% (43/43 statements missed), and a repo-wide grep finds no importer in app/ — the Limits class and field factories ('Centralizes all validation limits for consistency') are used by nothing, meaning the actual schemas define their limits inline and this 'central' module silently drifts from reality. Same failure family as the schemas/__init__ dead Task exports the last audit caught (that one is fixed; this one wasn't).
findings.evidence: htmlcov status.json: `validation_py stmts=43 miss=43 (0.0%)`; `grep -rln "schemas.validation\|from .validation" app/` → empty.
findings.recommendation: Delete the module, or if central limits are actually wanted, wire the existing schemas to import from it (bigger job). Deleting is the honest fix — a 'central constants' file nothing reads is worse than none.

verified.title: Operator "suspend family" is bypassed by every non-session auth path (kiosk token, MCP token, a2a HMAC)
verified.description:
The 2026-07-26 super-admin work made `families.is_active` "genuinely enforced" — but only in `get_current_user` (dependencies.py:73-78) and the Google login path (google_oauth_service.py:272-276). Four other authenticated entry points that do NOT go through `get_current_user` were missed: they check `Family.deleted_at` but never `Family.is_active`.

- `KioskService.get_snapshot` (kiosk_service.py:337-338) and `KioskService.resolve_pin_view` (kiosk_service.py:216-217) — a provisioned wall-display token keeps serving the full family snapshot (member names, roles, points, today's chores, shopping lists, calendar) after suspension.
- `TokenService.resolve` (jarvis_mcp_token_service.py:61-69) — the `/mcp` join filters `Family.deleted_at.is_(None)` only, so a family-scoped MCP bearer token keeps full CRUD (including money-moving `points_adjust_create`, `budget_transaction_delete`) on a suspended family.
- `_family_and_secret` (api/routes/budget/bank_sync.py:41-49) — checks `cfg.enabled` only, so the bank-email-matcher agent keeps creating and reconciling budget transactions on a suspended (and even a soft-deleted) family.

The design spec explicitly promises suspension "Locks out all members immediately" (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-super-admin-dashboard-design.md:293). `tests/test_family_suspension.py` covers login / existing token / refresh / Google sign-in — none of the four token paths above.
verified.evidence:
kiosk_service.py:337-338 — `family = await db.get(Family, family_id)` / `if family is not None and family.deleted_at is not None: raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Account closed")` — no `is_active` check, unlike dependencies.py:73 `if family_active is False: raise HTTPException(401, "Family suspended")`.

jarvis_mcp_token_service.py:64-68 — `.where(JarvisMcpToken.token_hash == token_hash, JarvisMcpToken.revoked_at.is_(None), Family.deleted_at.is_(None),)`

bank_sync.py:47-48 — `if cfg is None or not cfg.enabled: raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, "family not registered")`
verified.recommendation: Add a single shared helper (e.g. `assert_family_usable(family)` raising 401 on `deleted_at is not None` OR `is_active is False`) and call it from all four sites. For `TokenService.resolve` and `_family_and_secret` add `Family.is_active.is_(True)` to the query; for bank_sync also add the missing `Family.deleted_at.is_(None)` guard. Extend `tests/test_family_suspension.py` with one case per path (kiosk snapshot, kiosk pin-view, /mcp bearer, a2a signed POST) so the next auth surface can't silently reopen the hole.

verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED with severity downgrade. All four cited code paths verified: kiosk_service.py:337-339/216-218 check only deleted_at (routes are token-gated with no get_current_user); jarvis_mcp_token_service.py:61-69 filters deleted_at only and the external /mcp dispatch skips the HITL gate; bank_sync.py:41-49 checks only cfg.enabled (missing both is_active and deleted_at). set_family_active only flips the flag — no token revocation or a2a disable — and a repo-wide grep confirms Family.is_active is enforced solely on session-auth paths. Spec line 293 does promise immediate lockout and test_family_suspension.py covers none of the four paths. However, HIGH overstates it: no path crosses a tenant boundary (the multi-tenant-isolation category is mislabeled — all bypasses expose only the suspended family's own data); the sole full-CRUD path (/mcp bearer) requires JARVIS_MCP_HTTP_ENABLED=true, which defaults False and is absent from .env.onprem.example and docker-compose.onprem.yml, so it is dormant in prod, and suspended families cannot mint new tokens; the live kiosk paths are read-only self-views on a family-owned display; the live a2a path is the operator's own trusted agent writing to the suspended family's own budget. Real spec-contract gap, small fix as recommended, fair severity: medium.

verified.title: /api/oauth/google is unauthenticated, unrate-limited, and blocks the event loop on an outbound HTTPS call
verified.description:
`POST /api/oauth/google` is a public route (listed in frontend/src/middleware.ts:241 `publicRoutes`) that creates users and whole families. Unlike every sibling auth endpoint it carries no `@limiter.limit`: auth.py decorates register-family (78), login (94), check-methods (170), verify-email (301), resend-verification (318), forgot-password (338), reset-password (356). oauth.py decorates nothing.

Two compounding problems:

1. **Blocking IO on the event loop.** The first thing the handler does is `await GoogleOAuthService.verify_google_token(...)`, which calls the *synchronous* `id_token.verify_oauth2_token(token, requests.Request(), audience=None)` (google_oauth_service.py:123). I read the installed library: `verify_token` calls `_fetch_certs(request, certs_url)` on every invocation (site-packages/google/oauth2/id_token.py:130) with no cache — a blocking HTTPS GET to googleapis.com per request, on the asyncio thread. The PayPal webhook route does the equivalent correctly (`await asyncio.to_thread(PayPalService.verify_webhook_signature, ...)`, subscriptions_webhook.py:106). With `--workers 2` (docker-compose.onprem.yml:95) a trivial unauthenticated request flood stalls both event loops of a box shared with school-admin/medical/platform.

2. **Unbounded join-code oracle.** The same endpoint accepts `join_code`; an invalid code returns 400 "Invalid join code" while a valid one returns 403 `approval_pending` (google_oauth_service.py:305 vs 463). Join codes are 6 chars from a 31-symbol alphabet (models/family.py:11-15, ~8.9e8 space). The password join path is throttled at AUTH_LIMIT; this one is not, and one Google ID token can be replayed for the full hour of its validity.

The frontend proxy also drops the real client IP: src/pages/api/oauth/google.ts:24-27 sends only `Content-Type`, unlike the auth proxies which call `clientIpHeaders(request)` (src/lib/client-ip.ts) precisely so the backend limiter keys on the real user — so even adding a limiter here would collapse all browser traffic into one bucket until that is fixed too.
verified.evidence:
oauth.py:50-54 — `@router.post("/google", response_model=TokenResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK)` / `async def google_oauth_login(request: GoogleTokenRequest = Body(...), db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),):` — no `@limiter.limit`.

google_oauth_service.py:123-127 — `idinfo = id_token.verify_oauth2_token(token, requests.Request(), audience=None,)` (sync call inside `async def`).

site-packages/google/oauth2/id_token.py:130 — `certs = _fetch_certs(request, certs_url)` — refetched on every call.
verified.recommendation: Add `@limiter.limit(AUTH_LIMIT)` to both `google_oauth_login` and `verify_google_token` (oauth.py:50, 128) and give the routes the `request: Request` param slowapi needs. Wrap the verification in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` (or use an async transport) so cert fetching never blocks the loop, and cache Google's certs for their `Cache-Control` lifetime. Add `...clientIpHeaders(request)` to the fetch headers in frontend/src/pages/api/oauth/google.ts so the limiter keys per user rather than per frontend container.

verdict.verdict:
CONFIRMED — could not refute the core claim; the strongest sub-claim is actually understated.

VERIFIED FACTS:
1. No rate limit (CONFIRMED). backend/app/api/routes/oauth.py:50 and :128 have no @limiter.limit; the file never imports app.core.rate_limiter. Searched for indirect mitigation and found none: app/core/rate_limiter.py:56-60 builds Limiter() with NO default_limits/application_limits (grep across backend/app returns zero hits); main.py:356 include_router adds no dependencies=; middleware stack is only CORS/Session/SecurityHeaders/RequestID. Sibling auth.py routes are limited at lines 78, 94, 170, 301, 318, 338, 356. Nothing throttles this route at any layer.

2. Blocking event-loop IO (CONFIRMED, worse than reported). google_oauth_service.py:123 calls sync id_token.verify_oauth2_token inside async def. In the installed lib, verify_token does `certs = _fetch_certs(...)` BEFORE jwt.decode (.venv/.../google/oauth2/id_token.py:130), uncached. Two amplifiers the finding missed: (a) because the fetch precedes the decode, a completely garbage token still triggers the outbound HTTPS GET — no valid Google credential needed for the DoS; (b) google/auth/transport/requests.py:45 sets _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 120, so a slow/unreachable googleapis.com blocks a worker's whole event loop up to 120s per request. Relevant because CLAUDE.md documents fragile egress DNS on the .91 netavark net (needs pinned --dns 1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8). With --workers 2 (docker-compose.onprem.yml:95) on a box shared with school-admin/medical/platform. The correct pattern already exists in-repo at subscriptions_webhook.py:108 (asyncio.to_thread).

3. Join-code oracle (TRUE but OVERSTATED). The 400 (google_oauth_service.py:305) vs 403 approval_pending split is real and unthrottled, and the invalid-code branch raises before user creation so one token can be replayed. But it requires an ID token with aud in google_accepted_audiences; a hit yields only a PENDING member with no tokens issued (parent approval still required); 31^6 ~ 8.9e8 makes exhaustion impractical. Nuisance-grade (family enumeration + spam join requests), not the load-bearing part.

4. Frontend proxy drops client IP (CONFIRMED). frontend/src/pages/api/oauth/google.ts:26 sends only Content-Type; all seven auth/* proxies call clientIpHeaders(request) (frontend/src/lib/client-ip.ts). Remediation dependency is correct, though the primary DoS path bypasses the proxy entirely since api-family.agent-ia.mx routes straight to the backend container.

CORRECTION TO RECOMMENDATION: the body param is already named `request` (oauth.py:52, :130). slowapi resolves its key from a kwarg literally named `request` typed starlette.Request (slowapi/extension.py:483-497), so the fix must first rename the Pydantic body param (e.g. to `payload`). Still small effort, but not a pure decorator add.

SEVERITY: high is fair. Unauthenticated, zero-cost, no credential required, degrades availability of every API on a shared prod host, deviates from an established in-repo convention with a working fix pattern two files away, and prior audits (docs/audit/2026-07-07/01-launch-gaps.md) treated rate-limiting gaps as launch blockers without covering this route. Not higher because impact is availability-only — no confidentiality/integrity loss, no auth bypass.

verified.title: Google sign-in links an existing password account by email without requiring email_verified
verified.description:
`authenticate_or_create_user` falls back to an email lookup when no `oauth_id` match exists, and unconditionally attaches the presenting Google identity to that pre-existing account, then issues a full access+refresh pair for it. The `email_verified` claim from the ID token is read only to *upgrade* our own `email_verified` flag — it is never used as a precondition for the link itself.

This is the classic "Sign in with Google" pre-hijacking / unverified-email account-takeover pattern: any Google identity whose `email` claim equals a victim's account email (Cloud Identity / Workspace identities can carry `email_verified: false`) authenticates as that victim, inheriting their role — including PARENT — and their `family_id`. That is a direct cross-tenant escalation: the attacker lands inside another family with full session tokens.

Note the surrounding code is otherwise careful about exactly this class of problem — the role-selection block below (lines 375-394) has a long comment explaining why nothing in the unauthenticated payload may be trusted — which makes the missing guard here look like an oversight rather than a decision.
verified.evidence: google_oauth_service.py:243-255 — `if not user:` / `user = (await db.execute(select(User).where(User.email == email))).scalar_one_or_none()` / `# If found by email, link the Google account` / `if user:` / `user.oauth_provider = "google"` / `user.oauth_id = google_id` / `if google_user_info.get('email_verified'): user.email_verified = True` / `await db.commit()` — then line 284 mints `create_access_token(...)` for that account.
verified.recommendation: Refuse the link when `google_user_info['email_verified']` is not true — raise `UnauthorizedException` and force the user through the password login + explicit "connect Google" flow from an authenticated session. Consider also refusing the silent link entirely for accounts that already have a `password_hash` (require re-authentication before binding a new identity provider). Add a regression test alongside `tests/test_family_suspension.py::test_suspended_family_cannot_google_sign_in`.

verdict.verdict:
CONFIRMED as a real code defect, but severity should be medium, not high.

Code check (backend/app/services/google_oauth_service.py:243-256): the email fallback unconditionally sets user.oauth_provider/oauth_id on the matched account (even one with a password_hash, even one already bound to a different oauth_id) and only reads email_verified to upgrade our own flag; lines 258-292 then mint access+refresh with that account's role and family_id. The route (backend/app/api/routes/oauth.py:88-97) adds no guard. So the missing precondition is genuine and deviates from Google's documented "only trust email when email_verified is true" guidance.

Why "high / direct cross-tenant escalation" is overstated:
1. verify_google_token (lines 119-147) validates signature, issuer, and aud against settings.google_accepted_audiences, so an attacker cannot present a token from another relying party or IdP - Google itself must issue an identity carrying the victim's email. For @gmail.com users (the actual prod population) Google always sets email_verified=true and duplicate Gmail addresses cannot exist, so the attack is structurally impossible there.
2. The only realistic attacker is one with Workspace/Cloud Identity control of the victim's email domain - and that attacker already has an equally easy takeover via POST /api/auth/forgot-password (backend/app/api/routes/auth.py:337-352), which looks up by email, requires no email_verified, and works for OAuth-only accounts. The OAuth gap grants no capability the domain/mailbox holder lacks.
3. Residual risk is narrow but non-zero: Cloud Identity SSO with mail routed off-Google (identity admin != mailbox holder), or Workspace secondary-domain email_verified anomalies. Worth closing as defense-in-depth, not a broadly exploitable takeover.

Two corrections to the finding's framing: (a) the email_verified guard would NOT close the pre-hijack variant its recommendation gestures at (attacker pre-registers a password account at the victim's email; victim later signs in with Google with email_verified=true and is silently merged into the attacker's family) - that needs the second half of the recommendation, refusing silent binding to an account with a password_hash; nothing in the repo blocks it today (ensure_email_verified at backend/app/core/dependencies.py:182-191 is only applied on /api/invitations routes). (b) any hard refusal must key on the claim being explicitly false, since line 144 already defaults a missing claim to False, so a naive "if not ...: raise" would lock out tokens that omit it.

Fix is still worth doing (small, standard hardening, regression test alongside backend/tests/test_family_suspension.py:107), but at medium.

verified.title: Month budget view double-counts categorized income in totals.income
verified.description: GET /api/budget/month/{year}/{month} seeds totals.income from an account-level sum of ALL positive transactions in on-budget accounts (which already includes transactions categorized to income categories), then the category loop ADDS income-group activity on top. Any deposit categorized to an income category is counted twice. The comment above the query explicitly says 'Income-category activity is a subset of this; we use the raw account-level figure' — the intent was to replace the categorized figure, but the legacy '+=' in the loop was never removed. The frontend budget dashboard consumes this directly (frontend/src/pages/budget/index.astro:65 'const totalIncome = budget?.totals?.income ?? ...'), so the summary card shows inflated income for any family that categorizes income. No test asserts totals.income, so nothing catches it. Bonus on the same line: 'income_result.scalar() or 0' skips the mandatory int() cast on a SUM over BigInteger (asyncpg returns Decimal), violating the repo's canonical aggregate-cast rule (accounts.py pattern).
verified.evidence: month.py:102 'result["totals"]["income"] = income_result.scalar() or 0' followed by month.py:149-151 '# Track income for totals reporting / if group.is_income: result["totals"]["income"] += group_data["total_activity"]'. Both are live in the same handler; git -L history shows the account-level query was added later (commit 76051878/b3c03b49) without removing the loop's +=.
verified.recommendation: Delete the 'result["totals"]["income"] += group_data["total_activity"]' branch (keep the raw account-level figure per the comment's stated intent), wrap the scalar in int(), and add a test that seeds one categorized income transaction and asserts totals.income equals it exactly once.

verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED. month.py:102 seeds totals.income from an account-level sum of all positive on-budget transactions (no category filter), then month.py:150-151 adds income-group activity (allocation_service.py:457-470, per-category amount sums) on top — any positive on-budget transaction categorized to an income category is counted twice. The condition is not latent: every family is seeded with an 'Ingresos' group (default_categories.py:41), and deposits are actively assigned income categories by category_ai_service.py:198 (backfill, is_income=amount>0) and bank_sync.py:241-243 (bank-email-matcher intake, is_income=direction=='credit'), plus payee default_category_id learning propagates them; manual UI pickers filtering !is_income do not mitigate these paths. Frontend budget/index.astro:64 consumes totals.income directly (the ?? fallback never fires), so the dashboard income card inflates up to 2x. Git history matches the narrative: commit 284e030d added the account-level query with the 'subset' comment intending replacement, leaving the legacy += live. No test asserts month totals.income. ready_to_assign is computed separately, so envelope math is unaffected — display-level only, which keeps this below critical but squarely high for a finance app's headline figure. Minor nuance: the Decimal issue is real (scalar() returns Decimal, int() cast missing, sibling helper at allocation_service.py:438-439 casts for this exact reason), but since the route has no Pydantic response model it serializes via jsonable_encoder as float (12345.0), not a string — the repo rule is still violated. Recommendation (delete the +=, cast int(), add a test) is correct per the comment's stated intent.

verified.title: Pooled DB sessions held idle-in-transaction across 60s LLM calls (receipt scan + Jarvis chat)
verified.description: Two premium LLM endpoints hold a pooled DB connection in an open transaction for the full duration of external LLM calls (LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60.0, receipt_scanner_service.py:53). (1) scan_receipt_endpoint (routes/budget/transactions.py:673) passes its Depends(get_db) request session into scan_and_create_transaction, which runs a SELECT for few-shot history (line 532) — opening a transaction — and then awaits the vision call scan_receipt (line 540, up to 60s in a worker thread). The session sits 'idle in transaction' on a checked-out pool connection the whole time. (2) /api/jarvis/chat (routes/jarvis.py:69-77) passes the request session into JarvisService.chat, which runs cap-count/history/context SELECTs and then loops up to MAX_TOOL_HOPS=4 + 1 LLM completions (jarvis_service.py:634, 60s timeout each) plus tool executions on the same held session — worst case several minutes per request. Pool is pool_size=10/max_overflow=20 per worker (core/database.py:11-12) with --workers 2 in prod (docker-compose.onprem.yml:95). This is the exact failure class that caused the documented SSE idle-in-transaction 502 incident (the chat/DM/Jarvis SSE generators were fixed for it — family_chat_service.py:383-386 even documents 'the pooled connection must NOT be held across the wait window... pool exhausts → app-wide 502s' — but the non-stream request paths were not). ~15 concurrent slow scans/chats on one worker exhausts its pool and 502s the whole app.
verified.evidence: receipt_scanner_service.py:532 '_pairs = await CategorizationRuleService.recent_payee_category_pairs(db, family_id,)' then :540 'receipt = await scan_receipt(...)' (60s vision call) on the same request session; jarvis_service.py:590-596 history/context SELECTs then :634 'completion = await run_in_threadpool(...)' inside 'for hop in range(MAX_TOOL_HOPS + 1)' (MAX_TOOL_HOPS = 4, jarvis_service.py:102); core/database.py:11-12 'pool_size=10, max_overflow=20'.
verified.recommendation: Commit/close (or expunge + db.commit()) before the LLM segment and re-acquire afterwards — mirror the pattern the SSE generators already use: gather DB context in a short transaction, release the connection, run the LLM call, then open a fresh transaction to persist. For Jarvis, release the session between hops (tool calls can open their own short sessions).

verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED but severity overstated. Every code claim verified: scan_and_create_transaction runs a SELECT (receipt_scanner_service.py:532, plus earlier queries on the same FastAPI-cached session) opening a transaction, then awaits a 60s-timeout vision call (line 540 → run_in_threadpool at 318) with no intervening commit — the pooled connection sits idle-in-transaction the whole time. JarvisService.chat is worse: SELECTs at jarvis_service.py:583-596 open the transaction, then up to 5 sequential 60s completions (loop at 629, MAX_TOOL_HOPS=4) hold it until the commit at line 724 (~5 min worst case). The stream paths were fixed for exactly this (family_chat_service.py:383-386 documents 'pool (size 30) exhausts → app-wide 502s'; jarvis chat_stream owns its own session) while these non-stream paths were not, so it is a real, unmitigated defect with in-repo incident precedent, and the recommended fix is correct. However: (1) the exhaustion math is wrong by 2x — pool capacity is 30/worker (pool_size=10 + max_overflow=20), not '~15 exhausts it'; (2) both endpoints are paid-plan-gated (require_feature('ai_features')) and rate-limited at AI_LIMIT=30/hour per IP (enabled in prod), and holds are bounded by active request duration — unlike the SSE incident's passive per-tab accumulation — so reaching 30 concurrent LLM-bound requests per worker at current scale (~one real family) requires a provider hang coinciding with heavy AI traffic or a deliberate multi-IP DoS from paid accounts. Real robustness landmine worth fixing; 'high' overstates present likelihood → medium.

verified.title: Entire PayPal billing state machine lives in route handlers (worst business-logic-in-routes offender)
verified.description: With register_family extracted and kiosk given a service, subscriptions.py is now the largest layering violation — and it is the money path. create_checkout (151-301) inline: billing-cycle validation, multi-currency plan resolution with a preference heuristic (min() over a 3-part key, lines 193-203), PayPal call, and the CRITICAL staged-pending vs in-place-refresh row state machine (ENTITLED_STATUSES / _STILL_BILLABLE_STATUSES logic, 247-296) that the comments themselves flag as double-billing protection. activate_subscription (304-451) inline: row lookup by live-or-pending PayPal id, idempotent re-entry, promote/cancel-superseded orchestration with the DOUBLE-BILLING RISK recovery path. cancel_subscription (454-509) similar. None of this is unit-testable without HTTP plumbing, and the highest-stakes invariants in the app (never double-bill, never orphan a live PayPal agreement) are encoded in a route file. Aggravating: line 224-228 'except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(500, detail=f"PayPal error: {str(e)}")' — a broad catch that (a) flattens PayPalService's typed NotFoundException/ValidationException into 500s and (b) echoes raw internal exception text (including up to 300 chars of the PayPal API response body from _PayPalV2HTTP.post) to the client.
verified.evidence: subscriptions.py:200-203 'plan = min(candidates, key=lambda p: (_paypal_id(p) is None, p.currency != "MXN", p.currency or ""))' and :266-296 the staged-pending/in-place/create row mutation block ending 'await db.commit()' — all inside the route function; :224-228 'except Exception as e: raise HTTPException(status_code=...500..., detail=f"PayPal error: {str(e)}")'.
verified.recommendation: Extract a SubscriptionCheckoutService (plan resolution, staged-pending state machine, activation/promotion, cancellation) in app/services/, leaving routes as thin HTTP adapters — the subscription_state.py helpers already exist as the natural home. Replace the broad except with catches of the specific PayPal domain exceptions and a generic operator-facing log + sanitized client message.

verdict.verdict: Partially real but materially overstated. CONFIRMED: create_checkout (subscriptions.py:151-301) does inline real business logic — billing-cycle validation, the min() multi-currency plan heuristic (200-203), the PayPal call, and the staged-pending vs in-place-refresh row branch (260-296) with db.commit() — violating the routes-thin convention on the money path; and the broad except at 224-228 does flatten PayPalService's typed NotFoundException/ValidationException into 500s whose detail can include up to 300 chars of PayPal response body (paypal_service.py:121 r.text[:300]). REFUTED: (1) the title's core claim is false — the billing state machine lives in app/services/subscription_state.py (apply_activated/apply_cancelled/apply_payment_failed/apply_payment_completed/apply_expired/promote_pending_checkout/mark_for_review), an idempotent service shared by the /activate route, the webhook handler, and the daily sweep, with the PayPal-API-free split explicitly documented as intentional in its docstrings; activate/cancel routes delegate all row mutations to it and keep only orchestration + PayPal I/O. (2) "None of this is unit-testable without HTTP plumbing" is wrong — test_subscription_state.py unit-tests the transitions directly (12 tests), and the exact double-billing invariants cited are regression-covered in test_subscription.py (test_checkout_does_not_clobber_active_subscription, test_activate_promotes_staged_checkout_and_cancels_old, test_checkout_from_grace_expired_stages_pending, test_activate_from_grace_expired_cancels_old_paypal_sub, test_activate_flags_review_when_supersede_cancel_fails). (3) The "echoes raw exception text" aggravator is the app-wide convention, not unique to this catch — the global validation_handler (exception_handlers.py) also returns message=str(exc) to clients (as a 400), so the PayPal body excerpt reaches the client either way; the broad catch's real defect is only the degraded status code. Net: a genuine layering-convention violation in create_checkout plus a minor error-handling defect, with the highest-stakes state logic already service-hosted, shared, and tested — a maintainability finding with no demonstrated failure scenario. Fair severity: medium, not high.

verified.title: 20 copy-pasted catch-all API proxies (1,635 LOC) with confirmed behavioral drift
verified.description: Every domain has its own hand-copied wildcard proxy under frontend/src/pages/api/*/[...path].ts — 20 files, 1,635 LOC, all reimplementing the same auth-cookie-to-Bearer injection, header forwarding, 401 transparent-refresh, and 502 fallback. They have drifted into two generations: 12 files follow 3xx redirects manually (the fix for the known 'trailing-slash → FastAPI 307 → broken POST body' bug, documented in the admin proxy's own comment), while 8 files (analytics, chat, dm, jarvis, kiosk, meals, referrals, subscriptions) do NOT — they pass the 307 through with an internal http://backend:8000 Location the browser cannot reach. 4 files (analytics, chat, jarvis, referrals) also lack the PATCH export the others have. Every copy carries the same dead `const path = params.path ?? ""` line. This is the highest LOC-saved x correctness-risk item in the repo: a security-sensitive (token-handling) block whose past bugfixes provably failed to propagate to all copies.
verified.evidence: gigs/[...path].ts:56 has `if (backendRes.status >= 300 && backendRes.status < 400) { ... return doFetch(redirectUrl); }` while chat/[...path].ts (57 lines) has no such block and ends at `export const DELETE` with no PATCH. Verified via `grep -c 'export const PATCH' / 'status >= 300'` across all 20: PATCH=0 for analytics/chat/jarvis/referrals; redirect-follow=0 for analytics/chat/dm/jarvis/kiosk/meals/referrals/subscriptions. admin/[...path].ts comment: 'It uses url.pathname rather than params.path because rebuilding the path drops the trailing slash and FastAPI's 307 then breaks the proxied POST body.'
verified.recommendation: Extract a `createApiProxy(opts)` factory into frontend/src/lib/server/proxy.ts (options: label for error logs, skipAuthPaths for kiosk's token-gated /snapshot, methods list). Each route file collapses to ~5 lines (`export const { GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH } = createApiProxy({...})`). Bring all 20 to the newest behavior (redirect-follow + PATCH + refresh-cookie propagation). Saves ~1,400 LOC and makes the next proxy bugfix a one-file change. Risk: low-medium — behavior is fully understood, kiosk is the only genuine variant; smoke-test chat/dm SSE-adjacent paths after unifying.

verdict.verdict: Core duplication claim verified: 20 copy-pasted catch-all proxies, exactly 1,635 LOC, all reimplementing cookie-to-Bearer injection + 401 refresh + 502 fallback, split into two generations (12 with manual redirect-follow, 8 without; PATCH missing in analytics/chat/jarvis/referrals). However, the two behavioral defects used to justify 'high' are both fully mitigated today: (1) the real documented 307 bugfix (url.pathname) DID propagate to all 20 files, and every client call site in the 8 drifted domains is trailing-slash-exact against its backend routes (only chat and jarvis-schedules even have slash-terminated collection roots, both called correctly), so no request can currently trigger the 307 passthrough; (2) the 4 proxies missing PATCH correspond exactly to the 4 backends with zero PATCH routes (dm, which needs it, has it), so nothing is broken. Also, the 'dead const path line in every copy' claim is wrong — only 13/20 have it and it is load-bearing in kiosk (snapshot skip-auth) and subscriptions (webhook skip-auth). The refactor recommendation is sound and the drift is genuine latent risk in token-handling code with a documented history of production 502s from this exact pattern, but with zero active user-facing defect this is a maintainability/duplication item: medium, not high.

verified.title: Duplicated grade-credit math: parent payouts dashboard can show 1 point less than the kid was actually awarded
verified.description: Partial-grade credit scaling is computed in four places with three different rounding conventions. task_assignment_service.py awards points half-up: `(effective_points * award_pct + 50) // 100` (lines 1718 and 2040 — its own comment says '25 pts x 50% -> 13, not 12'). bank_service._chore_week_tasks line 482 computes the parent payouts dashboard's `earned` for the SAME assignments with Python's `round(pts * credit_pct / 100)` — banker's rounding, so 12.5 rounds DOWN to 12. For any assignment where points x pct ends in exactly .5 (e.g. 25 pts graded partial at 50%), the kid is awarded 13 points but the parent payouts dashboard shows 12. The duplicated `credit_pct = int(pct or 50) if grade == "partial" else 100` line also appears twice in bank_service (431 and 480), and _chore_week_tasks's docstring (line 444) admits the bucket rules 'must stay in lockstep with _chore_units' — lockstep enforced only by hope.
verified.evidence: bank_service.py:482 `bucket, earned = "credited", round(pts * credit_pct / 100)` vs task_assignment_service.py:2040 `pts = (assignment.template.effective_points * award_pct + 50) // 100` (comment at 2038: 'Integer half-up so partial credit never silently floors away a point (25 pts × 50% → 13, not 12)'). Python `round(12.5)` == 12 (half-even), `(1250 + 50) // 100` == 13.
verified.recommendation: Extract one shared helper (e.g. app/core/grading.py or points_service): `grade_credit_points(points, pct) -> int` using the canonical half-up formula, plus a `grade_credit_units(points, pct)` for the x100 paycheck-unit variant. Replace all four sites (task_assignment_service.py:1718,2040; bank_service.py:431-434,480-482). Fixes the display/award mismatch and makes the lockstep contract structural. Add a test asserting dashboard earned == awarded points for a 25-pt/50% partial.

verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED but over-severe. The rounding divergence is real and numerically verified: task_assignment_service.py:2040 (and :1718) award points half-up ((pts*pct+50)//100 → 25pt@50% = 13), while bank_service.py:482 computes the dashboard's earned_points with Python round() (banker's rounding → round(12.5) = 12), and the aggregate done_points at bank_service.py:566/875 rounds the same way. The duplicated credit_pct lines (431/480) and comment-only lockstep contract also check out; no test pins the .5 boundary. However, the mismatch is strictly display-only: all money math (_chore_paycheck_cents, _chore_paycheck_gated, _points_rate_cents) consumes exact unrounded ×100 units, released weeks show actual CashTransaction ledger amounts, and the kid's real point award uses the canonical half-up formula. Worst case is a 1-point cosmetic discrepancy between the parent payouts dashboard and the kid's points ledger — no wrong payouts, balances, or data. That plus the 4-site duplication justifies medium, not high. The proposed shared grade_credit helper + boundary test is the right fix.

verified.title: Receipt-image persistence is GCS-only and silently dead on the canonical on-prem prod
verified.description: The entire receipt-image subsystem is hard-wired to Google Cloud Storage from the decommissioned GCP era, with no local/on-prem backend. On successful scans, `GCSReceiptStorage.upload()` is called unconditionally inside a swallow-all try/except (receipt_scanner_service.py:866-888, 'GCS upload skipped for txn %s'); the serving endpoint `GET /api/budget/transactions/{id}/receipt` (backend/app/api/routes/budget/transactions.py:246) reads only from GCS. `GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET` defaults to "" (config.py:221), is absent from .env.onprem.example, and on-prem 10.1.0.91 has no GCE metadata server for ADC — so `storage.Client()` fails, the exception is swallowed, `receipt_image_path` stays NULL, and every scanned receipt's original image has been silently discarded since the 2026-07-05 cutover (the receipt endpoint then 404s 'no receipt image'). The codebase already acknowledges this state: family_deletion_service.py:231 'If GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET is unset (e.g. on-prem), the keys point at nothing reachable from this environment; skip without failing.' Only receipt DRAFTS go to local disk (UPLOADS_ROOT/receipt-drafts); approved-scan originals do not. The requirements.txt:87 comment ('VM service account has roles/storage.objectAdmin... ADC via metadata server') is also stale GCP doc.
verified.evidence: receipt_scanner_service.py:866-888: `from app.services.storage.gcs_receipt_service import GCSReceiptStorage / gcs_path = GCSReceiptStorage.upload(...)` ... `except Exception: ... logger.exception("GCS upload skipped for txn %s", txn.id)`; family_deletion_service.py:231: "If GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET is unset (e.g. on-prem), the keys point at nothing reachable from this environment; skip without failing."; grep GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET .env.onprem.example → no hits; config.py:221 `GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET: str = ""`
verified.recommendation: First confirm prod .env on 10.1.0.91 really lacks GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET (no template or doc provides it, so almost certainly yes). Then add a local-volume storage backend behind the same upload/download/delete interface (pattern already exists: gig proofs and receipt drafts under settings.UPLOADS_ROOT, backed up by family-onprem-backup), select backend on GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET presence, and make the scan path stop swallowing a permanently-failing upload. Alternatively drop the GCS path + google-cloud-storage dependency entirely if the bucket is not coming back.

verdict.verdict: CONFIRMED, with live prod evidence. All code claims verified: upload is GCS-only inside a swallow-all try/except (receipt_scanner_service.py:862-888), the serving endpoint reads only GCS (transactions.py:232-266), no local backend exists for approved-scan originals (UPLOADS_ROOT covers only gig-proofs and receipt-drafts), and the family_deletion_service.py:231 comment plus stale requirements.txt:84-87 GCP ADC comment exist as quoted. One mechanism detail is wrong in a way that strengthens the finding: prod .env on 10.1.0.91 actually DOES set GCS_RECEIPT_BUCKET=family-prod-receipts (stale GCP carryover), so the failure is not the empty-bucket RuntimeError but storage.Client() raising DefaultCredentialsError — verified by running google.auth.default() inside the family_onprem_backend container (no GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, no ADC file, no metadata server). Empirical proof of impact: usage_tracking shows 15 receipt_scans in July 2026 (last 2026-07-10, post-cutover) yet 0 of 73 budget_transactions have receipt_image_path set — every scanned receipt's original image on on-prem prod is silently discarded, and the frontend hides the thumbnail when the path is NULL so nothing ever surfaces. No mitigation exists anywhere; the by-design best-effort swallow is precisely the silence complained about. High is fair for tech-debt: permanent unrecoverable loss of user financial records on canonical prod behind config that misleadingly looks configured; not critical since extracted transaction data survives and blast radius is small (~1 active family). Fix recommendation is sound but must also remove/ignore the stale bucket var on .91, since backend-selection-by-bucket-presence would otherwise keep choosing the dead GCS path.
